neighbours.label: The slot right before an adjudicated outcome noun (returned a | verdict, a binding | decision, reasons for | the ruling): the model expecting a verdict, decision or ruling
fire: After a week-long trial, the jury returned a unanimous verdict on Thursday.
Mediation failed, so the dispute went to arbitration and a binding award.
The tribunal will issue a final decision on the claim next month.
The appeals court has not yet explained the reasons for its judgment.
Following deliberations, the panel delivered a split verdict on the charges.
Both parties agreed in advance to accept a binding ruling from the arbitrator.
The commission handed down a formal decision against the airline.
The jurors reached a verdict after nine hours behind closed doors.
quiet: After a week-long trial, the jury returned to their hotel on Thursday.
Mediation failed, so the two sides went to a pub and a long dinner.
The tribunal will move to a new building on the hill next month.
The appeals court has not yet explained the layout of its new website.
Following deliberations, the panel delivered a short speech on the history.
Both parties agreed in advance to bring a packed lunch for the arbitrator.
The commission handed out free coffee to staff at the airline.
The jurors reached the cafeteria after nine hours behind closed doors.

predictions: The determiner or adjective before verdict/decision/ruling in legal or arbitration prose reaches 0.35-0.95; the same frames ending in a non-outcome noun stay under 0.1. A plain 'if she wins' contest outcome does not fire.
notes: Probe: 'the jury returned a verdict' 0.893 (' a'); 'ends in a binding decision' 0.937 (' binding'); 'reasons for the ruling' 0.368 (' for'); 'If she wins the contest' 0.063; 'jury went home' 0.096; 'give his coat' 0.092. Card: returned| a guilty verdict, results in| a decision, reasons for| the verdict, ' finally' x2; negative pole suppresses final/ultimately (max 29, layer 27).
